reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Bedrock cost accounting can underestimate billable input tokens when an explicit cache-point TTL differs from the configured cache setting, requiring effective-TTL weighting and a regression test.
1 open issue - [Cost weighting ignores TTLs on explicit cache points](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/478#discussion_r4519563923) · New
What changed in this PR This PR updates Bedrock Converse token accounting to include cache writes in reported input tokens and costs, aligning Claude weighting with the Anthropic provider. **Changes:** - Count cache-write tokens with model-specific multipliers, treating a missing field as zero. - Add response-parsing tests for Claude cache durations, Nova, and missing cache-write usage. - Document the accounting change in the changelog. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `tests/​test_provider_bedrock_converse.py` | Adds cache-write token accounting tests. | | `chatlas/​_provider_bedrock_converse.py` | Includes weighted cache writes in input token totals. | | `CHANGELOG.md` | Documents corrected Bedrock token and cost reporting. |
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended Cache-write costs can be underreported because concurrent requests overwrite shared TTL state, and TTL scanning misses tool-config and tuple-content cache checkpoints.
1 open issue - [Keep cache TTL metadata request-scoped](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/478#discussion_r4519630896) · New
2 previously missed issues In code that hasn't changed since last review
Include tool-config blocks when scanning cache points `chatlas/​_provider_bedrock_converse.py:379` Converse also accepts cache points in `toolConfig.tools`, but this helper scans only system and message blocks. A Claude request using `cache="none"` with an explicit 1h tool-cache checkpoint therefore records no TTLs and counts its cache writes at 1.25x instead of 2x. Please include tool-config blocks in the scan.
Scan tuple message content for cache points `chatlas/​_provider_bedrock_converse.py:383` This skips explicit cache points when a message's `content` is a tuple. Such content is preserved by `_chat_perform_args` when it already contains a cache point, and `converse_wire_value` serializes tuples as JSON arrays, so the request can successfully use a 1h checkpoint while its writes are counted at 1.25x. Please scan tuple content as well as lists.
1 resolved since last review - [Cost weighting ignores TTLs on explicit cache points](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/478#discussion_r4519563923)
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended Lost request-specific TTL metadata and incorrectly weighted mixed-TTL cache writes cause inconsistent token counts and inaccurate cost accounting.
1 open issue - [Preserve request TTL metadata for completion accounting](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/478#discussion_r4519684137) · New
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Account for cache writes using their TTL-specific rates `chatlas/​_provider_bedrock_converse.py:778` With `cache="auto"`, an explicit 1h system checkpoint is combined with an automatically appended 5m message checkpoint. If the system prefix is a cache hit and only the 5m suffix is written, this branch weights all writes at 2x instead of 1.25x, reporting 900 rather than 600 input tokens for 100 uncached input tokens plus 400 written tokens. Use TTL-specific write usage where available; otherwise avoid automatically introducing mixed TTLs and handle explicit mixed-TTL requests without presenting the maximum-rate estimate as exact accounting.
1 resolved since last review - [Keep cache TTL metadata request-scoped](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/478#discussion_r4519630896)
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended The added tests do not verify explicit cache-TTL propagation through synchronous and asynchronous streaming, leaving a gap where a 1h override could silently use the configured 5m rate.
1 open issue - [Add streaming tests for explicit cache TTL propagation](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/478#discussion_r4519721544) · New
1 resolved since last review - [Preserve request TTL metadata for completion accounting](https://github.com/posit-dev/chatlas/pull/478#discussion_r4519684137)
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: Do other providers need to incorporate cache write tokens?

Good question. Anthropic already folds cache writes in. Checking the rest: OpenAI does need it, since GPT-5.6 and later bill Responses cache writes at 1.25x (2.5x for the 12h lifetime) and report them as `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`, which is included in `input_tokens`. That is in a separate PR, #480, so this one stays Bedrock-only. Google reports no write count, Ollama is local, and the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions providers (OpenRouter etc.) expose the field but the write rate depends on the upstream model, so I left those out.

`_chat_perform_args()` preserves caller-provided cache points, so `self._cache` can differ from the TTL actually sent to Bedrock. With `cache="none"` and an explicit system cache point using `ttl="1h"`, 100 input tokens plus 400 cache-write tokens are reported as 600 rather than 900 billable input tokens, underestimating cost. Derive the weighting from the effective cache TTLs or TTL-specific response usage, and add a regression test for explicit cache-point overrides.

`Chat.__deepcopy__()` shares the provider across forks, so concurrent requests with different cache TTLs can overwrite this field before an earlier response is parsed. A 1h request followed by a 5m request then counts the first response's cache writes at 1.25x instead of 2x, underreporting its cost. Carry the TTL metadata with the corresponding response or stream accumulator rather than storing the latest request's TTLs on the provider.

Removing the TTL metadata makes token and cost extraction from a stored completion disagree with the turn when a request overrides the configured TTL. With `cache="none"`, an explicit 1h checkpoint, 100 input tokens and 400 cache-write tokens, the turn records 900 input tokens, but `value_tokens(turn.completion)` returns 600 and `value_cost(turn.completion)` uses that lower count. Retain the request-specific TTL information so subsequent accounting stays consistent.

The explicit-TTL test attaches this metadata manually, and none of the added tests exercises its propagation through a streaming request. The tests would therefore still pass if the synthetic chunk were dropped during merging or the TTLs were omitted from the final completion, causing an explicit 1h override to fall back to the configured 5m rate. Please add mocked synchronous and asynchronous streaming tests with `cache="none"`, an explicit 1h cache point, and nonzero cache-write usage; assert both the turn's tokens and `value_tokens(turn.completion)`.

Added in 9b2a9a22: `test_converse_stream_leads_with_cache_point_ttls` and its async counterpart assert the synthetic TTL chunk leads the stream for an explicit 1h cache point with `cache="none"`, and `test_stream_turn_retains_cache_point_ttls` asserts the TTLs survive `stream_merge_chunks` → `stream_turn` and that `value_tokens(turn.completion)` agrees with the turn.'s recorded tokens (900 input tokens for 100 + 400×2.0).

On the mixed-TTL summary point: Bedrock reports a single aggregate `cacheWriteInputTokens` with no per-TTL breakdown, so exact attribution is impossible when a request mixes TTLs (only reachable when the caller injects explicit cache points alongside the auto-appended message point). The code takes the 1h rate in that case — documented in `value_tokens()` — preferring a bounded overestimate over underbilling. Suppressing the auto-appended message cache point whenever the caller places explicit points would avoid the mix, but silently changes caching behavior (fewer cache hits) for a rare accounting edge case.
